quiz.q: According to the Supreme Court in the S.R. Bommai case (1994), what is the only valid method to determine whether a state government has lost its legislative majority?
options: A mandatory floor test conducted inside the state legislative assembly.
A subjective assessment report submitted confidentially by the state Governor.
A formal physical verification of legislators conducted before the President.
A special investigation committee constituted by the Inter-State Council.
quiz.why: The Supreme Court ruled that a floor test in the legislative assembly is the only constitutional way to test a ministry's majority. Subjective gubernatorial assessments cannot justify invoking Article 356.

quiz.q: Under Article 252, what makes the surrender of state legislative power over a State List entry particularly consequential for the resolving states?
options: The central legislation remains valid only for a temporary duration of one year.
The consenting states surrender their executive authority to implement the central statute.
The statute automatically applies to all non-consenting states without their formal approval.
The resulting central law can subsequently be amended or repealed solely by Parliament.
quiz.why: When two or more states pass resolutions under Article 252, legislative authority transfers permanently to Parliament for those states. The states cannot subsequently amend or repeal the resulting parliamentary statute.

quiz.q: In Hargovind Pant v. Raghukul Tilak (1979), how did the Supreme Court characterize the constitutional position of the Governor?
options: The Governor functions as an administrative agent subordinate to the Union executive.
The Governor occupies an independent constitutional office and is not a Union employee.
The Governor serves as an ombudsman authorized to oversee state assembly affairs.
The Governor acts as a central representative directly accountable to national Parliament.
quiz.why: The Supreme Court affirmed that the Governor holds an independent constitutional office of dignity. Even though appointed by the President, the Governor is neither an employee nor a subordinate agent of the Union government.

quiz.q: What limitation did the Supreme Court place on the President's pleasure doctrine regarding the removal of Governors under Article 156?
options: Governors can only be removed through a formal parliamentary impeachment procedure.
Governors must always receive a mandatory hearing before any removal decision.
A change of central government or ideological differences cannot justify arbitrary removal.
Governors enjoy a fixed five-year term that cannot be cut short.
quiz.why: The Supreme Court ruled that while the President can remove a Governor without a hearing, the pleasure doctrine cannot be exercised arbitrarily. Neither a change in the central government nor differing political ideologies constitutes a valid ground for dismissal.
